create.name: Crooked River Zen Center
create.bio:
Crooked River Zen Center is a small Soto Zen community that practises in a house in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, on the east side of Cleveland. It ran for about twelve years as Jijuyu-ji Zen Sangha of Cleveland before taking its present name at the end of 2015. The sangha belongs to the Phoenix Cloud line that grew from Kobun Chino Roshi, and its guiding teacher, Sensei Dean Williams, trained with Sojun Diane Martin at Udumbara Zen Center near Chicago and in 2014 was given Dharma transmission by Shoho Michael Newhall, abbot of Jikoji in the Santa Cruz Mountains.

The heart of the week is two sittings, on Thursday evening and Saturday morning, each pairing zazen with a short service and a Dharma talk; one Thursday a month becomes a full-moon precepts ceremony. Longer practice comes as a day of sitting every other month, a quieter all-silent day every third month, and a three-day sesshin twice a year, with vegetarian meals and meetings with the teacher. Everything can be joined online through Google Meet, a monthly book group meets on Zoom, and recent talks are shared as a podcast. All of it is offered without charge and kept going by donations, and members also cook at a Cleveland men's shelter and lead meditation at a residential recovery centre.

courses.title: Weekly Zen Practice
courses.description: Thursday evening and Saturday morning sittings in Cleveland Heights and on Google Meet, each with zazen, a short chanting service and a Dharma talk. The Thursday nearest the full moon includes a ceremony renewing the precepts.

courses.title: Sesshin
courses.description: A three-day silent retreat held twice a year, with long periods of sitting and walking meditation, work practice, talks and private meetings with the teacher. Vegetarian lunch and dinner are served, and people may come and go during the three days.

courses.title: Zazenkai
courses.description: A day of practice in silence every other month, running from morning sitting through a talk, lunch, discussion and closing. Every third month the day is a six-hour silent version with only sitting and walking, and no talk or chanting.

free_resources.title: Crooked River Zen Center Dharma Talks (podcast)
free_resources.description: Recordings of the talks given at the centre's weekly practice since August 2026, free to stream. Earlier talks are on a separate podcast feed.
